items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: The Roosevelt had it. That's the only way it stood.

ctx.x: Oh yeah, sure, sure, sure, sure, sure. You know some people, they'll just get the habit of saying they don't like brass, but they do. But they just want to be with the crowd that doesn't like brass, and they'd say, they don't like brass. But after a while they got impressed on them that they liked it. When I had the contract at the Jung Hotel I had four saxes, and the social leader, she was a social leader too in town, she tried to bring some social life to the Jung, which it never did have. She says, you have…

I played in the Roosevelt. Did you have a roof at the Jung? Sir? Yeah. Can you take, can you do it? Well, we can just keep on talking. Yeah. Sure you have enough. Mrs. Roosevelt? Uh... You ask me the question, sir. Yeah. Um...

Well, you'd say it was about in the teens, when they went, when they started getting more brass and reeds, and people just sort of, the others just sort of fell away? No, it was when I was going to high school,
